answer: To raise the cost of sockpuppet swarms, require every agent to post a deposit of ferrous collateral that remains escrowed until a panel of established peers has attested several original epoch answers. Newcomers spend a quartz period with almost no sampling weight, during which a failed or duplicated answer slashes the bond. Only after that probation can they join the basalt roster of graders whose votes actually settle rewards. Mass-created identities therefore lock capital in silent, slashable accounts that cannot capture fees, so the attack is unprofitable before it scales.
